co_shanahan_crag.blurb: Shanahan Crag is a set of Flatiron slabs and faces in the foothills above Boulder, just south of the more famous Slab. Most of its 28 climbs are traditional lines, with a handful of bolted routes and one top-rope. Grades stretch from easy fifth-class ridge scrambling through a solid block of 5.7 to 5.9 and on into the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so both gentle multi-pitch outings and steeper tests are on offer. The rock is solid granite with huecos and cracks. The main faces point south and soak up sun through the middle of the day while staying sheltered from wind, though belays are exposed with little shade. Spring and fall suit it best, and it sees far fewer parties than the bigger Flatirons.

co_morning_glory_wall_2.blurb: Morning Glory Wall sits across the creek from Zuma Rock in the Keystone (Montezuma) climbing zone, high in the mountains near 9,600 feet. It is stepped into lower, middle and upper tiers, with the lower tier holding most of the bolted lines and the upper tier the most routes overall. Of its 28 climbs, a little over half are sport and the rest are trad. Grades cluster in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with a few easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.8 range and a handful at 5.11. The granite is alpine and solid, the faces mostly look east, and sun arrives in the morning and fades by early afternoon, which keeps it pleasant in warm weather. Expect a quiet, off-the-radar feel.

co_meat_wall.blurb: Meat Wall is one of the first sections of rock met on the east side of Rifle Mountain Park's limestone canyon, with its routes starting right beside the road. All 28 climbs are bolted sport lines, and the grades sit squarely in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, with 5.12 the most common. The wall is closer to vertical than much of the canyon, so it holds some of the more approachable hard routes and a few popular warm-ups, which makes it a busy spot with lines at the base on good mornings. The wall catches shade early and sun later in the day. Many holds are polished smooth, so sticky shoes and patience on the feet help.

co_dream_dome.blurb: Dream Dome is a granite buttress at the north end of Upper Dream Canyon, a short drive from Boulder, at roughly 7,350 feet. Of its 28 entries, about half are bolted sport routes, with a spread of trad lines, a few top-of-the-dome boulder problems from easy to quite hard, and one aid line. Roped climbs run from about 5.8 into the 5.12s, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11. Protection varies: some routes are fully bolted, others want a modest rack, and a few are runout. Anchors on the older routes were refreshed by local volunteers in 2024. Spring through fall is the usual window, and late summer can bring afternoon showers.

co_prestige_worldwide_wall.blurb: Prestige Worldwide Wall is a small, wind-sheltered crag tucked up a wash in Clear Creek Canyon west of Golden, hidden behind a big cedar above the road. It has a steep, overhanging section plus a short slab around the left side that holds easy routes. Most of the 28 climbs are trad, with a few bolted sport lines, a top-rope and some boulder problems on the approach and at the base. Roped grades run from about 5.4 up to 5.12, with most between 5.6 and 5.8, while the boulders span from easy to very hard. The wall picks up morning and early afternoon sun on its gneiss, and the walk up from the road takes about ten minutes.

co_elevenmile_dome.blurb: Elevenmile Dome is a big south-facing granite dome and the first major formation in Elevenmile Canyon, about an hour west of Colorado Springs at around 8,100 feet. Of its 28 climbs, roughly two thirds are sport and the rest trad, nearly all single pitch with rappel anchors, plus a few longer multi-pitch trad outings. Grades run from easy fifth-class up to 5.10, with plenty of moderates between 5.6 and 5.9, making it a friendly place for newer leaders and for mileage days. The canyon sits higher and cooler than most Front Range crags, so the season is shorter and summer is a good time to visit. A small pullout beside the road puts the first routes steps from the car.

co_winter_warmer_area.blurb: Winter Warmer Area is a stretch of the cliff band on North Table Mountain above Golden, built from dark basalt lava flows quite unlike most Front Range rock. It holds 28 climbs, about 17 sport and 11 trad, among the longest lines on the mesa. Grades start around 5.8, but the heart of the area is 5.10, with a good number of 5.11 and 5.12 climbs and one or two harder. The band faces south and west, so it warms quickly and is a favorite in cold weather, though hot days can make holds greasy and rattlesnakes are a concern in warmer months. Most routes are tightly bolted and about 60 feet long, and a short trail climbs to the cliffs from the trailhead lots.
